thread.title: Brewers Beat Dodgers 6-4 in NLCS Game 4 to Reach World Series After 44 Years
thread.title_full: Brewers Beat Dodgers 6-4 in NLCS Game 4 to Reach World Series After 44 Years

author: latimes
title: Brewers Beat Dodgers 6-4 in NLCS Game 4 to Reach World Series After 44 Years
text:
Milwaukee Brewers defeated Los Angeles Dodgers 6-4 in NLCS Game 4 on October 15, 2026, advancing to their first World Series since 1982 and ending the Dodgers' title defense.
The Milwaukee Brewers defeated the Los Angeles Dodgers 6-4 in Game 4 of the National League Championship Series on Thursday, October 15, 2026, at Dodger Stadium in Los Angeles. The win sends Milwaukee to the World Series for the first time in 44 years, since 1982, and ends the Dodgers' bid for a third consecutive championship.
Dodgers fans left Dodger Stadium with long faces, while Brewers supporters stayed celebrating for several minutes after the 27th out. The Dodgers, accustomed to celebrating in the past two years, had no smiles in their clubhouse, only words of resignation at the postgame press conference.
Dodgers Manager Reflects on NLCS Loss
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts addressed the media after the defeat. He said he was very proud of his players but acknowledged the pain of not reaching the World Series. Roberts stated he told the team he was proud, though he is not used to giving consolation speeches, and called it still a good season.
Roberts said he had no regrets about his decisions in the NLCS, where the Dodgers did not win a single game. He credited the Brewers, saying they played flawlessly and that his team gave everything but it was not enough. He noted that Milwaukee had the best record in baseball and won four games.
The Dodgers held leads in all four games of the series. In Game 4, Milwaukee had to come back from a 4-0 deficit. Roberts expressed that he would have liked to go to the World Series and defend the title, but the Brewers are the ones advancing.
Shohei Ohtani Struggles in Postseason
Shohei Ohtani was clearly not at his best this postseason. A year ago, in Game 4 of the 2025 NLCS, Ohtani almost single-handedly sealed a sweep over the Brewers with three home runs. In this Game 4, Ohtani hit his first home run in nearly two months and his first of the postseason.
The previous night, he had been dropped to sixth in the batting order in Game 3, as the Dodgers considered benching him due to injuries to his right biceps and left knee, which he had been dealing with since at least June. Roberts said the home run was good and gave them a chance, adding that he will always trust Ohtani, calling him the best player on the planet, but noted he was not at 100 percent.
Roberts emphasized that it was about the whole team and not just one player who did not perform. The Dodgers were 2 for 11 with runners in scoring position. Tyler Glasnow pitched 4.1 innings, allowing 4 earned runs with 6 strikeouts.
Season Overview and Manager Milestone
When discussing the season and the manner of elimination, Roberts said it had nothing to do with player fatigue or age. He dismissed the idea that age was a factor. Roberts completed his sixth season with 100 wins, tying Joe McCarthy and Bobby Cox as the manager with the most such seasons in Major League history.
The Dodgers finished the regular season with a 100-62 record and won the National League West by nine games. It was their first 100-win season since 2023 and the 12th in franchise history. However, in the NLCS, their star-studded rotation of Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, and Tyler Glasnow could not secure a win against the Brewers.
The Brewers' victory marks a historic moment for the franchise, as they return to the World Series for the first time in 44 years. The Dodgers, who had won the past two World Series, will now watch from home as Milwaukee competes for the championship.
